title: Information Diet
hook: Three hours of business content every week and you can't name one thing it changed.
statement: Be picky about what you read, watch, and listen to.
explainer: A so-so feed you check five times a day crowds out the great source you only get to weekly. It's not about consuming less. It's protecting time for what's worth it.
sop: List every regular input: feeds, newsletters, podcasts, people you follow.
Score each source's Quality from 1 to 10 and log its Time per week.
Unsubscribe or mute the bottom half.
Keep a queue for good sources so you read them on purpose.
Re-audit quarterly. Useful then can be noise now.
equation_example: Source A: Quality 8 ÷ 2 hours = 4.0. Source B: Quality 2 ÷ 6 hours = 0.33. Higher means it earns its spot. Lower means it's eating time better stuff could have had.
question: Name the one input you consume daily that's pure junk, and cut it this week.
closing_statement: Low-quality inputs still cost you real time.
